To find the physical dimension of the resulting quantity, we start with the definition provided in the problem:

1.  **Identify the inputs and their dimensions:**
    *   Luminous intensity ($I$): The problem specifies its dimension as **Luminosity**.
    *   Power ($P$): Power is defined as energy per unit time. Energy has the dimension of $\text{Mass} \times \text{Length}^2 / \text{Time}^2$. Therefore, power has the dimension:
        $$\text{Dimension}(P) = \frac{\text{Mass} \times \text{Length}^2}{\text{Time}^2 \times \text{Time}} = \frac{\text{Mass} \times \text{Length}^2}{\text{Time}^3}$$

2.  **Calculate the dimension of the resulting quantity (luminous efficacy):**
    The problem defines this specific quantity as luminous intensity divided by power:
    $$\text{Dimension}(\text{Result}) = \frac{\text{Dimension}(I)}{\text{Dimension}(P)}$$
    Substituting the dimensions we found:
    $$\text{Dimension}(\text{Result}) = \frac{\text{Luminosity}}{\left(\frac{\text{Mass} \times \text{Length}^2}{\text{Time}^3}\right)}$$

3.  **Simplify the expression:**
    To simplify, multiply by the reciprocal of the denominator:
    $$\text{Dimension}(\text{Result}) = \frac{\text{Luminosity} \times \text{Time}^3}{\text{Mass} \times \text{Length}^2}$$

<ANSWER>Luminosity * Time^3 / (Mass * Length^2)</ANSWER>
